title: The Night Owl
logline: The foggiest night of the year, and the lighthouse keeper is a tiny old owl who cannot keep her eyes open. A ferry is feeling its way toward the rocks. {product} keeps the light on.

world.setting: Point Hollow, a fictional rocky island lighthouse off a stylized New England coast, one foggy night until sunrise. Inside: a cosy round lamp room with a giant brass and glass lens, a knitted blanket on a stool, a small wooden ice crate. Outside: black rocks, rolling fog, and the little night ferry Marigold with warm cabin windows.
world.palette: Colour script built from the can: sky blue fog and silver moonlight for the problem, warm amber lamp light as the character accent, and the can's gold sun as the sunrise payoff.
fictional_brands: Point Hollow Light (the lighthouse, white tower with a sky-blue band, no lettering)
Marigold (the night ferry, cream hull with a sky-blue stripe, the name is spoken only, never painted)
world.rules: Every hull, sign, crate and chart is blank. The can is the only real brand and the only photoreal object. The owl is an adult elder; no children in the story.

beats.summary: Mabel's huge eyes droop shut as the lamp behind her flickers; she tells herself to stay awake.
Outside, the beam is dying in the fog while the ferry creeps toward the rocks; the captain radios in; Mabel jolts awake.
She lifts the can out of the ice crate (up to her chin), cracks it, sips, and her eyes pop wide. The brand line.
She throws her whole body on the crank, the lens roars to full blaze, the beam slices the fog and the ferry turns away from the rocks.
The ferry passes safely below, passengers wave lanterns, Mabel waves back from the gallery.
Sunrise: the can on the gallery ledge, Mabel finally asleep in her blanket beside it. Tagline.

music.brief: A sleepy celeste and music-box lullaby in F major, 72 bpm, with a low cello note that keeps dragging it flat as her eyes close; a pizzicato sting on the jolt awake.
The lullaby melody pops into a bright staccato pizzicato version at 110 bpm on the can crack, playful, leaving room for her line.
Full orchestral lift of the same melody: strings and French horns swell as the lens blazes, a heroic brass statement as the ferry turns, then warm strings under the wave.
Back to the celeste lullaby, soft and resolved, a final glockenspiel twinkle on the tagline.
